{{Short description|Dutch mathematician (born 1953)}}
'''Frits Beukers''' ({{IPA|nl|frɪts ˈbøːkərs}}; born 1953 in [[Ankara]], Turkey) is a Dutch mathematician, who works on [[number theory]] and [[hypergeometric function]]s.

In 1979 Beukers received his PhD at [[Leiden University]] under the direction of [[Robert Tijdeman]] with thesis ''The generalized [[Ramanujan–Nagell Equation]]'', published in ''[[Acta Arithmetica]]'', vol. 38, 1980/1981. From 1979 to 1980 he was a visiting scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref>[http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/ Institute for Advanced Study: A Community of Scholars]</ref> He became a professor in Leiden and in the 2000s at [[Utrecht University]].

Beukers works on questions of [[Transcendental number|transcendence]] and [[Irrational number|irrationality]] in number theory, and on other topics.   In connection with the famous proof by [[Roger Apéry]] (1978) on the irrationality of the values of the [[Riemann zeta function]] evaluated at the points 2 and 3, Beukers gave a much simpler alternate proof using [[Legendre polynomials]]. He also published on questions in mechanics about [[dynamical system]]s and their exact solvability.
